title: Automated Investigation, Response and Automatic Attack Disruption

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)
Manage automated investigation and response capabilities in Microsoft Defender XDR; configure automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Automated investigation and response (AIR)

AIR examines an alert, collects evidence, gives each piece of evidence a verdict and proposes or takes remediation actions.

Item Fact
Covers Devices (Defender for Endpoint), on-premises AD users (Defender for Identity), email (Defender for Office 365)
Verdicts Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found
Approval Actions that need approval wait in Action center > Pending
Approve with Security Administrator, or the unified RBAC permission Security operations \ Security data \ Response (manage)
Bulk approval Multi-select works for actions of the same type
Level that controls it The automation level of the device group (Module 3)

Documented change: since September 1, 2026, AIR no longer runs as a separate investigation experience or manual trigger for Defender for Endpoint alerts. AIR for Defender for Office 365 remains. Learn the Action center workflow; it is the same place where all response actions are approved.

Exam tip

. Pending = waiting for a person. Full automation = no approval. Approvals live in the Action center, with Pending and History tabs.

2The Action center

Tab Use
Pending Approve or reject actions; select several of the same type
History Audit log of completed actions; undo is possible for some

Action sources include manual device action, manual email action, automated device action, automated email action, advanced hunting action, Explorer action and live response action. Path: Actions & submissions > Action center.

3Automatic attack disruption

Automatic attack disruption stops active, fast-moving attacks such as ransomware campaigns by containing assets the moment the attack is recognized, with high confidence. All automatic actions can be undone.

Action Product that applies it
Contain device Defender for Endpoint (blocks traffic to and from the device)
Contain IP for undiscovered devices Defender for Endpoint
Contain user Defender for Endpoint (enforced at the endpoint; also used by predictive shielding)
Isolate device Defender for Endpoint (automatic isolation is in preview)
Disable user Defender for Identity (cloud-only accounts through the managed app Microsoft Defender for Identity)
Revoke user session, suspend user Microsoft Entra ID
OAuth app compromise Defender for Cloud Apps
Safeboot hardening, GPO hardening, proactive user containment Predictive shielding

Okta and AWS disruption (through Sentinel) is in preview.

Exam tip

. Attack disruption contains; it does not clean up. After containment the analyst investigates and undoes the actions when needed.

4Prerequisites

Area Requirement
License Microsoft 365 E5/A5 or Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 among other qualifying products
Device discovery Standard discovery (needed for contain device)
Device group The automation level must not be No automated response
Contain user Sense agent version 10.8470 or later
Defender for Identity Auditing on domain controllers; action accounts (default LocalSystem)
Defender for Cloud Apps Microsoft 365 connector with all boxes selected, including Microsoft Entra ID apps
Defender for Office 365 Mailboxes in Exchange Online; audit events MailItemsAccessed, UpdateInboxRules, MoveToDeletedItems, SoftDelete, HardDelete

Turn it on in Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features > Configure automatic attack disruption. Roles that can configure it include Global Administrator, Security Administrator and Security Operator.

5Seeing what disruption did

Where What you see
Incident queue The tag Attack Disruption
Incident page A yellow banner
Activities tab A Policy status column
Action center An entry for each action, with undo
Advanced hunting Table DisruptionAndResponseEvents (preview)

6Exclusions

Path: Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response.

Tab Exclusion
Identities Add user exclusion (for example a break-glass account)
Devices > Device groups Set the automation level per group; excluding a group also affects AIR
Devices > Policy application Create rule against a tag; Exclude IP

Permissions: with unified RBAC off, Security Administrator or Global Administrator; with it on, Security Operator or Core security settings (manage). A full opt-out needs a support case titled Attack disruption opt-out; Microsoft does not recommend it.

Exam tip

. Exclude a break-glass or critical service account with a user exclusion, not by turning the feature off for everyone.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Automatic attack disruption contained a device and disabled a user during a suspected ransomware attack. The analyst finds a false positive. What is the right next step?

  • AOpen a support case to remove the tenant license
  • BWait for the actions to expire after exactly seven days of review
  • CDelete the incident so the actions are rolled back
  • DReview the Action center and undo the containment actions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Every automatic attack disruption action can be undone from the Action center.

S2A break-glass administrator account must never be disabled by automatic attack disruption. What should be configured?

  • AA suppression rule under Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression page
  • BA user exclusion under Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response
  • CA device group with the automation level set to Full for all devices
  • DAn opt-out of attack disruption for the whole tenant by support case
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Identities tab of Automated response has Add user exclusion.

S3A device group is set to No automated response. What is the effect on automatic attack disruption for the devices in that group?

  • AContainment still runs because it ignores the automation level
  • BContainment runs only after a person approves each action
  • CContainment is not applied because the prerequisite is not met
  • DContainment runs only for the users that signed in on the devices
Show the answer

Answer: C. The device group automation level must not be No automated response.

S4An analyst filters the incident queue for incidents where Microsoft acted automatically to contain an attack. Which tag should the analyst look for?

  • ARedirected, which marks a merged incident
  • BDefender Experts, which marks incidents under managed hunting
  • CAttack Disruption, which marks contained attacks
  • DCritical asset, which marks high value devices
Show the answer

Answer: C. Incidents where attack disruption acted carry the Attack Disruption tag.

S5Fifty pending file quarantine actions of the same type are waiting. The analyst wants to approve them quickly. What should the analyst do?

  • AReject all of them and run each one again manually
  • BOpen each device page and approve every action separately
  • CMulti-select the actions of the same type in Action center > Pending
  • DRaise the automation level and wait for the next scan to run
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Pending tab supports multi-select for actions of the same type.

S6Automatic attack disruption must disable a cloud-only user account. Which component performs the action?

  • AThe managed enterprise app named Microsoft Defender for Identity
  • BThe Windows LocalSystem account on every domain controller
  • CA playbook that calls the Microsoft Graph API on demand
  • DThe Defender for Cloud Apps session policy engine on the reverse proxy
Show the answer

Answer: A. Cloud-only accounts are disabled through the Microsoft-managed enterprise app Microsoft Defender for Identity.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What are the three AIR verdicts?

Show the answer

Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found.

R2Where are pending remediation actions approved?

Show the answer

Action center > Pending.

R3Which device discovery mode does contain device need?

Show the answer

Standard discovery.

R4Which minimum sense agent version does contain user need?

Show the answer

10.8470.

R5Where are attack disruption exclusions configured?

Show the answer

Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response.

R6Which hunting table records disruption events?

Show the answer

DisruptionAndResponseEvents (preview).

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
AIR verdicts Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found; approve in Action center > Pending
Change since September 1, 2026 no separate AIR experience for Defender for Endpoint alerts; AIR for Office 365 remains
Disruption actions contain device, contain IP, contain user, isolate, disable user, revoke session, OAuth app
Prerequisites E5 or Plan 2, standard discovery, automation level not No automated response
Visibility tag Attack Disruption, yellow banner, Action center, DisruptionAndResponseEvents
Exclusions Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response
